notes: Draw every sprite at scale 0.5 (or load as @2x/resolution 2). Ground anchor (0.5,0.5) on the tile centre from toScreen(i,j); objects anchor (0.5,0.75) on the tile centre. Layers: ground < overlay < object (sort objects by i+j).

shore.rule: bit set when that neighbour is land. Clear a corner bit if either adjacent edge bit is set (N needs NW,NE clear; E: NE,SE; S: SE,SW; W: SW,NW). Reduced mask 0 = plain water; else file shore_<mask>.

shore_sand.appliesTo: water tiles whose land neighbours are beach sand
shore_sand.bits: same as shore (8-bit, corners reduced, 47 tiles)
shore_sand.rule: Compute the reduced shore mask exactly as for shore. Then count the land neighbours that set a bit in the reduced mask: if strictly more of them are sand than grass, use shore_sand_<mask>; otherwise (tie, majority grass, or any non-sand land) use shore_<mask>. Reduced mask 0 = plain water_a/b. Its land side has the same flat sand border as sand_a, so it meets sand_a and sand_edge_* seamlessly; water/foam/shallows match shore_* exactly, so shore and shore_sand tiles can sit side by side along the water.

sand_edge.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is sand OR water (water counts as sand so the beach runs to the shoreline). Mask 15 -> sand_a; else terrain/sand_edge/sand_edge_<mask:02d>@2x.png (mask 0 = lone sand patch). Open sides fade into the shared grass background ~0.2 tile inside the tile with an irregular border, so the tile edge on an open side is plain grass and meets grass_a..f seamlessly. 4-bit set: no diagonal bits, so an inside corner where only the diagonal neighbour is grass stays sand.

forest_edge.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is also forest. Mask 15 -> any of forest_a..d (interior); else forest_edge_<mask:02d> (trees thin out to bushes toward open sides; mask 0 = lone copse). Object layer over a grass tile, anchor (0.5,0.75).

road.crosswalks: on every arm of T (3-arm) and cross (4-arm) pieces
road.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is road; mask 0 has no sprite (use a dead-end).

road_dirt.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_concrete.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_stage_surveyed.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_stage_graded.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_stage_gravel.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_stage_surfacing.rule: bit set when that neighbour connects (any road set or stage). mask 0 = isolated.

road_asphalt.rule: v3 refreshed asphalt; same mask scheme. Legacy road_NN_* set kept.

street_asphalt.rule: 20 m per tile. 4 lanes x 3.0 m (12 m asphalt = 0.60 tile), 1.75 m sidewalks, no parking. Lane centres +-0.075 and +-0.225 tile from the centre line (right-hand: inner lane 0.075, outer 0.225).

street_concrete.rule: 20 m per tile. 4 lanes x 3.0 m (12 m asphalt = 0.60 tile), 1.75 m sidewalks, no parking. Lane centres +-0.075 and +-0.225 tile from the centre line (right-hand: inner lane 0.075, outer 0.225).

avenue_asphalt.rule: 20 m per tile. One carriageway per tile: 3 lanes x 3.2 m (carriageway 9.6 m = a 0.45-0.93), 1.4 m half-median on the partner edge (2.8 m median total; matches the game's AV_D0/AV_D1), 1.75 m sidewalk, grass verge. Lane centres 0.15, 0.31 and 0.47 tile from the median line (shared edge of the two halves) = 0.08, 0.24, 0.40 tile from the median curb. Right-hand traffic: inner (fast/left-turn) lane 0.15. Set the bit toward the partner half as well as along the road: a 3-bit mask = straight half, median on the odd arm, sidewalk on the missing side. 15 = open intersection; 0/1/2-bit masks use the street layout.

avenue_concrete.rule: 20 m per tile. One carriageway per tile: 3 lanes x 3.2 m (carriageway 9.6 m = a 0.45-0.93), 1.4 m half-median on the partner edge (2.8 m median total; matches the game's AV_D0/AV_D1), 1.75 m sidewalk, grass verge. Lane centres 0.15, 0.31 and 0.47 tile from the median line (shared edge of the two halves) = 0.08, 0.24, 0.40 tile from the median curb. Right-hand traffic: inner (fast/left-turn) lane 0.15. Set the bit toward the partner half as well as along the road: a 3-bit mask = straight half, median on the odd arm, sidewalk on the missing side. 15 = open intersection; 0/1/2-bit masks use the street layout.

avenue_extras.profile: verge a<0.3625 | sidewalk 0.3625-0.45 (1.75 m) | carriageway 0.45-0.93 (3 x 3.2 m; lane edges 0.45/0.61/0.77/0.93, dashed lines 0.61/0.77; white edge line ~2 px at a 0.46-0.48) | half-median 0.93-1.0 (1.4 m). Lane centres 0.15 / 0.31 / 0.47 tile from the median line = game AV_LN; median curb 0.07 = AV_D0, outer curb 0.55 = AV_D1.
avenue_extras.LR: Standing in the tile facing the partner edge P: L = counter-clockwise edge, R = clockwise edge (clockwise order NE->SE->SW->NW). Partner NE: L=NW, R=SE; SE: L=NE, R=SW; SW: L=SE, R=NW; NW: L=SW, R=NE.

kinds.end_<P>_<L|R>:
half enters through edge L/R and ends; median stops, lanes open across P into the partner end tile (U-turn). Pair: end_

_ with the partner end tile entering from the same edge direction.
kinds.corner_<P>_<L|R>: INNER half of a 90-degree bend: enters through L/R, leaves through the edge opposite P; medians on P and opposite L/R.
kinds.corner_outer_<N|E|S|W>: OUTER half of the bend (diagonal tile of the 2x2 bend block). Vertex = tile corner nearest the inner tile. The two other outer tiles of the bend are ordinary halves.
kinds.tee_<P>: side street joins on the outer edge (opposite P); median break + turn arrows. Put gap_<partner> on the far half.
kinds.gap_<P>: median break only (far half opposite a tee).
kinds.cross_<P>: a street crosses the avenue: street on the outer edge, median break, crosswalks + stop bar. Use cross_ on both halves; streets continue on both outer edges.

avenue_extras.example_bend: avenue along j (i=3 partner SE, i=4 partner NW) turning toward +i: (4,6)=corner_NW_R, (3,7)=corner_outer_E, (3,6)=half mask 7, (4,7)=half mask 11, then (i,6)=mask 14 / (i,7)=mask 11 for i>=5.
avenue_extras.note: Avenue meets 2-lane roads: the street (12 m) profile is used on the outer edge; legacy road_* tiles are 10 m-era and do not match.

avenue_taper.naming:
D = edge toward the narrower road; P = this tile's partner (median) edge, perpendicular to D; role main = the half the narrow road continues from (road centred on this tile), side = its partner half (ends in grass at D). Pair: ...__

_main with ...___side.
avenue_taper.rule: Use on the LAST avenue cell pair before a narrower road. For an avenue half tile with partner bit pd: for an along bit D (D != pd, D != opp pd) with (m & D) and neighbour rw < 2 (street or 2-lane): role=main. For its partner tile (partner at opp pd): if the main tile's D neighbour is narrow and its own D neighbour is not a road, role=side. kind = 'dirt' when that narrow neighbour is rw 0 and tier dirt, else 'street' (street rw 1, and paved 2-lane, which already draws street_<tier> via the jn rule). Tier = the avenue's tier. Skip the avenueLanes overlay on taper tiles. For kind dirt, do NOT apply the jn paved-apron rule to the dirt tile beyond: road_dirt_<mask> joins directly.
avenue_taper.geometry: Pair across-coord c from the median line (+ toward main's outer edge; main tile c 0..1, side -1..0); t 0 at the avenue edge -> 1 at edge D; s = smoothstep((t-0.08)/0.84). Median line 0 -> 0.5 (main tile centre). Main outer curb 0.55 -> 0.8 (street) / 0.93 (dirt); side outer curb -0.55 -> 0.2 / 0.07. Median 0.07 half-width closes by s 0.45 (nose ~t 0.45), then double yellow. 3 lanes per direction until s 0.42 (t ~0.45), then 2 lanes; inner lane line slides from 1/3 to 1/2 of the carriageway. Lane DROP is the outer (curb) lane of one direction: the main half's direction if D == R(P_main) (i.e. the main half's traffic flows toward D), otherwise the side half's direction; merge arrows in that lane at t 0.18 and 0.40. Last 30% of the tile crossfades into the street/road_dirt art (dirt: markings end at t 0.75). Vehicles: outer lane (0.47 from median) merges into middle lane by t 0.45; at t=1 the 2 lanes per direction sit at the street lanes (+-0.075/+-0.225 from road centre, street) or a single lane each way (dirt, +-0.15).
avenue_taper.LR: Same as avenue_extras: R(P) = clockwise neighbour of P (NE->SE->SW->NW).

vehicleBodyNote: Vehicle collision/body fields (rev v3-soft3d-l). Travel axis = the vehicle's facing direction on the iso grid. bodyFront/bodyRear: signed distance in TILES (1 tile = 20 m) along the travel axis from the sprite anchor (vehicle ground centre) to the front/rear bumper; front positive, rear negative. lengthTiles = bodyFront - bodyRear (true bumper-to-bumper length, measured from Blender geometry incl. lamps, cross-checked against rendered alpha). Bumper-to-bumper queue: centre distance between follower F and leader L = F.bodyFront - L.bodyRear + gap, i.e. place F anchor at L anchor - (F.bodyFront - L.bodyRear + gap) along the axis. travelAxisPx = screen offset in 2x px for +1 tile along travel (SE [64,32], SW [-64,32], NE [64,-32], NW [-64,-32]); divide by 2 for 1x screen px. headlightOffsetPx/taillightOffsetPx = bodyFront/bodyRear * travelAxisPx, in 2x px from the vehicle anchor: put the anchor of headlightGlow/taillightGlow (fx_*, blend add, layer night) there. Both fx glows are ground light: draw them UNDER the vehicle sprites (drawOrder 'underVehicle'). A taillight glow drawn over the body puts red light on the box/cab side and reads as a reversed vehicle. The sprite canvas is NOT centred on the body (anchor x != 0.5) - never space cars by canvas width.
